<description>
**Problem:** While the best header is at least a day old, a node normally selects one peer for initial headers sync.
An inbound or manual peer can answer with valid empty `headers` and remain selected, so another eligible peer is not asked.
Empty `headers` may mean that the peer is caught up with the node or stuck at the same height, so the response is not misbehavior.
When no other preferred download peer is available, the headers timeout will not release the peer, and automatic outbound eviction does not apply.

**Fix:** Release an inbound or manual peer from initial headers sync after an empty response while the best header is stale and cancel its download deadline, allowing another eligible peer to take over.
Restart the normal response window when releasing the slot so the same peer is not immediately selected again.
A new block announcement can still trigger the existing one-shot request.
Automatic full-relay and block-relay peers keep their existing headers timeout and old-chain eviction behavior.

Manual reproducer

Both runs use the checked-out `build/bin/bitcoind`, with the downloaded Python script supplying only two inbound P2P peers.

```bash
{ cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j10 --target bitcoind; } >/dev/null 2>&1
build/bin/bitcoind -regtest -daemonwait -datadir="$(mktemp -d)" -connect=0 -listen=1 -port=18455
time python3 <(curl -fsSL https://gist.github.com/l0rinc/39e471dd6835fe332205d3812ebb9e92/raw)
killall bitcoind
```

The fixed node returns as soon as the replacement peer receives `getheaders`.
On the old node, that wait times out after 10 seconds because the initial peer is still treated as active.

Fixes #34096
</description>

[2026-09-18] r:5249679243 review COMMENTED by mzumsande (member):
Some observations:
- this is not an attack. Any peer could just send nothing instead of sending an empty header and stall until the timeout hits. So this is more about interactions between honest nodes.
- Empty header messages are sent by Bitcoin Core itself not only when we have no more headers, but also when the node is below `minchainwork`. I think this is important information that belongs into the OP.
- `ConsiderEviction` is just one of two timeout mechanisms. `m_headers_sync_timeout` applies to all peers.
- #34096 is not a permanent stall to my understanding due to `m_headers_sync_timeout`, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/34096#issuecomment-5731625703
- Even if the stall was permanent, we'd just sync from another peer as soon as a new block is found, see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/0e9018e8b65611b0769545e177110e4b7fc51244/src/net_processing.cpp#L4413-L4422.

I would say that there are two separate possible problems, none of which are critical:
1.) headerssync can finish early before we get to the today -1 threshold because our peer's chain is not far enough. This could happen due to an empty message or a non-full message, it could happen after or before `MinChainWork` is reached (so we may have a HeadersSync object or not). In this case, it is strictly unnecessary to wait for the timeout. Instead, we could have a shortcut, in which we release the current sync peer immediately, give it a refractory period, so that we can sync from another peer. But nothing here is specific to inbound/manual peers, plus we might as well not do it and wait ~10 minutes for the next block instead.

2.) When `m_headers_sync_timeout` hits and we do not have a preferred peer (which means we are in a very bad situation anyway), we do nothing. Instead, we could reset  `nSyncStarted`, and possibly add a refractory period (this is optional in my opinion) so we could try sync from another non-preferred peer (e.g. an inbound).

I'm not sure about the current approach because it
- unnecessarily adds a restriction to inbound/manual peers to the empty-headers case, when full outbounds would benefit from it just as well. I don't think resettting ConsiderEviction is so important here, we just need headers from someone to start IBD!
- only addresses one of multiple possible paths in which we can return early from headers sync.
</new_statements>
